how: The built 0.4.0 package's helper, started against a throwaway store, with the real Codex Desktop program and the real Decisions API on the owner's dedicated API project. Nothing was installed and the installed 0.3.1 helper, its store and its settings were not touched. The throwaway store was deleted afterwards.

benchmark.note: One computer, one moment, a handful of calls. Not a latency guarantee and not evidence of routing quality.

main_turns.what: a short, specific question about one file
a multi-file review for races and isolation mistakes
a follow-up in the same task (routed after the first turn finished)
a request to delegate one lookup to a subagent
an explicit model choice (no Decisions call)
an explicit model choice, delegating one lookup

subagents.what: spawned inside composer task C, named list_every_caller_of_parse_response_read_only_lookup
spawned inside composer task C2, named print_first_line_of_one_named_file_trivial_read_only_lookup

results.superseded_note: These are the 2026-10-07 acceptance results. launch_readiness holds what was verified on the installed copy on 2026-10-08.

findings: Of the four composer turns that asked Decisions during acceptance, one was selected (confidence 0.78) and three fell below the 0.6 threshold (0.39, 0.52, 0.31) and took the local default under the rule in force at the time. That rule has since been replaced; see 'decided'.

Both subagent spawns carried an encrypted task message, so Decisions saw only the task name. It returned low confidence (0.49) once and abstained (0.50) once. The local default was written into the spawn and the child ran with it. A Decisions-selected subagent has still not been observed.

Shell commands failed in every live task with Codex's own Windows sandbox error 'helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors'. Codex's sandbox log shows the same error for the Desktop app's own sandboxed sessions since 2026-10-06 evening: its setup cannot update permissions on a Codex runtime file that another process holds open. This is independent of Gearshift and of which model ran, and routing and verification were unaffected by it. Running a composer task that executes commands successfully has therefore not been observed on this computer.
not_claimed: behavior on any other Codex version

after_acceptance.why: The owner asked for a decision on the confidence threshold. One call was made to see what a real uncertain answer contains, and one to try the resulting rule through the installed command line.

uncertain_answer.what: the same large task as the benchmark, classified as a main turn
uncertain_answer.under_the_old_rule: below 0.6, so the local default gpt-6.1-sol / medium, although only 0.21 of the estimate says a preset that light is enough
uncertain_answer.under_the_new_rule: cautious pick sol_deep (gpt-6.1-sol / xhigh), covering 0.67 of the estimate. Computed by replaying this answer through the shipped rule, not by a further call.
uncertain_answer.note: The confidence field (0.37) is not the same number as the top probability (0.46).

installed_command_line_route.what: gearshift route with the same task, on a fresh connection, 1500 ms deadline
installed_command_line_route.result: timed out at 1502 ms, so the local default was applied and labeled as a timeout fallback
installed_command_line_route.meaning: The deadline and the labeled fallback behaved as designed. It did not exercise the new rule live. The command line opens a new connection for every call; the helper uses its pooled one.

decided.confidence_rule: Kept min_confidence at 0.6 and changed what happens below it. At or above it, the top choice is used as before. Below it, Gearshift takes the cautious pick: never lighter than the top choice, and heavy enough that min_confidence of the estimate says a preset that heavy or lighter is right. With no usable breakdown it takes the heavier of the top choice and the local default. Labeled 'cautious', never 'selected'.
decided.powershell_hook_wrapper: Kept. It costs about 280 ms per hook, but it exists because a direct command failed on an earlier Codex build, a replacement cannot be tried on the real host without the owner trusting new hook definitions, and a mistake would stop routing altogether.

launch_readiness.how: The installed 0.4.0 helper on the owner's computer, with its real store, the real Codex Desktop program and the real Decisions API. Tasks were submitted to the running helper the way its local page submits them. The package under test is the one a release builds; its hook definitions are byte-identical to the installed, trusted ones.

decisions_calls.note: The 15-call budget in max_requests covered the 2026-10-07 acceptance. The owner then asked for the remaining gaps to be closed for launch, which needed live calls. Codex's own installed checks on 2026-10-07 account for the calls between 10 and 14.

coding_task.what: Create a small module and its tests, run the tests, fix until they pass. Then a follow-up adding a second function with two more tests.
coding_task.access: Full access, for one scratch folder. Codex's own Windows sandbox was refusing every sandboxed command on this computer; see codex_sandbox.
coding_task.checked_independently: node --test in that folder afterwards: 8 tests, 8 pass, 0 fail
coding_task.note: The first call took 2020 ms on a fresh connection. Under the earlier 1500 ms composer deadline it would have been a timeout fallback, not a selection.

first_attempt_with_default_access.what: The same coding task with Access left on the Codex default
first_attempt_with_default_access.outcome: Codex resolved the default to a workspace-write sandbox for this folder. Its sandbox setup failed, the command was refused with exit code -1, and nothing was written. Routing and verification were unaffected.

subagent.where: Inside a composer task whose main model was chosen explicitly, so only the subagent was classified
subagent.not_observed: A Decisions-selected subagent spawned from a chat in the Codex app itself. It is the same hook; the app spawns recorded earlier were routed by a fallback.

sandbox_label.what: A task limited to This folder, explicit model, asked to run one command
sandbox_label.page: The command line reads 'did not run: Codex could not set up its Windows sandbox', and the composer shows what Codex recorded and that Full access does not use the sandbox.

codex_sandbox.since: the Codex update of the evening of 2026-10-06 (program folders 979a96ce184041d1 and 9691020b546a15b2, both 0.162.0-alpha.2). Earlier program folders in the same logs show no failure.
codex_sandbox.codex_says: runtime read/execute validation failed ... node_repl.exe: open ACL target for root-only update: The process cannot access the file because it is being used by another process. (os error 32)
codex_sandbox.cause: Inferred, not read from Codex's source. That file is one of Codex's own runtime programs and the Codex app keeps it running. Opening it for reading works; opening it for writing fails with exactly this error, as Windows does for any running program. The read and execute permission the check is validating is already present on the file. So the check appears to open a running program for writing.
codex_sandbox.shown_without_gearshift: codex sandbox cmd /c type <file> fails with 'windows sandbox failed: helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors'. The same command with -c windows.sandbox="unelevated" prints the file.
codex_sandbox.gearshift_now: gearshift doctor warns; the composer explains it and labels each refused command. Gearshift reads only what Codex wrote to its own sandbox log and starts nothing to find out.

fresh_install.how: The downloadable zip, extracted and installed with its own installer into an empty profile: USERPROFILE, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA and CODEX_HOME all pointed at a temporary folder holding only a copy of the Codex program. No Node and no npm on the path.
fresh_install.command_line_without_npm: gearshift.cmd doctor and status worked with the bundled runtime
defects_found_and_fixed: Windows PowerShell stopped the installer on any line Codex wrote to its error stream. On a first installation Codex writes one when asked to remove a plugin that is not there. The installer now judges Codex by exit code.
A profile with no Startup folder made the installer fail. It now asks Windows for the folder without requiring it to exist, and creates it.
not_covered: reading the model list from a signed-in Codex

start_at_sign_in.real_profile: Helper stopped, then the Startup shortcut opened through Explorer, outside any assistant's process tree. One helper came up and routing resumed.
start_at_sign_in.fresh_profile: Same, with the shortcut the installer had just created.
start_at_sign_in.not_observed: An actual sign-out or restart of Windows.
